timeOfDayFinding.verdict: PRIMARY finding of the week. Runs that start at or after 17:00 UTC pay a ~45% penalty, and that penalty IS the p90 tail.
evidence: gated median 247s (<17Z) vs 357s (>=17Z), +110s / +45%. Pooled gated p90 for the week is 360s, i.e. the p90 is essentially the evening median.
e2e 'Build' step median 50.5s (<17Z) vs 148s (>=17Z), 2.9x. All 5 runs with Build > 100s started between 17:11Z and 20:06Z; the other 29 runs span 4s..98s with no gap.

The slowdown is NOT confined to e2e: web Build 52 -> 65 (+25%), web run tests 88.5 -> 105.5 (+19%), worker Build 41 -> 48.5 (+18%) in the same bucket. corr(e2eBuild, hour) = 0.56; corr(e2eBuild, webRunTests) = 0.53.
runnerWait is 4-14s in every single run including the slow ones, so this is NOT queueing for a runner. 'install dependencies' is 1-2s all week, so it is not pnpm store coldness either.
timeOfDayFinding.hypothesis: GitHub Actions cache-service throughput, not code. The e2e job writes a fresh ~hundreds-of-MB entry on nearly every run: key is runner.os-nextjs-e2e-<hash(pnpm-lock)>-<hash(web/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx})>, so the exact key changes whenever any web source file changes, and the run falls back to restore-keys. 'Post Cache Next.js builds' takes 8-21s on every run, i.e. a new entry is saved every time. With ~45 merge_group runs/day plus ~175 pull_request runs/day all writing turbo and Next.js entries, the repo cache budget churns through the day and late-day runs restore a worse fallback. UNPROVEN — there is no cache-API reader in the toolset and no log access this week to confirm hit/miss.
timeOfDayFinding.whyNoDiff: The fix lives in .github/workflows/pipeline.yml (cache key/path/save conditions, around lines 1417-1427), which this workflow is forbidden to edit even temporarily. Handed to a human as a report-only recommendation.
